title: Triple Sugar Iron (TSI) Test
principle: TSI agar contains three fermentable sugars (glucose at a low concentration, plus lactose and sucrose at higher concentrations), a pH indicator (phenol red), and an iron source (ferrous sulfate) to detect hydrogen sulfide production. Fermentation patterns, gas production, and blackening from H2S are read together from a single stabbed-and-streaked slant.
purpose: A widely used screening test for identifying and differentiating Enterobacteriaceae based on carbohydrate fermentation pattern, gas production, and hydrogen sulfide production, in one combined tube.
reagents: TSI agar slant (glucose, lactose, sucrose, phenol red indicator, ferrous sulfate/sodium thiosulfate for H2S detection)

procedure.instruction: Using a straight inoculating needle, stab the butt of the TSI slant to about two-thirds its depth, then withdraw and streak the slanted surface in a zig-zag pattern.

Incubate with the cap loosened slightly, at the appropriate temperature/duration for the organism (commonly read at a relatively short, standardized incubation window since prolonged incubation can cause a false reversion of the slant color as aerobic organisms exhaust the small glucose supply and begin oxidizing peptones).
Read the slant color, the butt color, presence of gas bubbles/cracks in the medium, and any blackening (H2S) together.

positiveResult: Interpretation is a combined pattern rather than a single positive/negative: e.g. an acid (yellow) slant and acid (yellow) butt indicates fermentation of lactose and/or sucrose in addition to glucose; an alkaline (red) slant with acid (yellow) butt indicates glucose-only fermentation; gas appears as bubbles or splits in the agar; blackening indicates H2S production.
negativeResult: An alkaline (red) slant and alkaline (red) butt with no gas or blackening indicates no fermentation of any of the three sugars under these conditions.
interpretation: TSI is read as a pattern (slant color / butt color / gas / H2S) rather than a single positive or negative outcome, and that pattern is combined with other tests for identification.

controls.organism: Salmonella enterica (acid butt, alkaline slant, gas, H2S positive is a commonly cited pattern for many Salmonella strains)
Escherichia coli (acid slant and butt, gas, H2S negative is a commonly cited pattern for many E. coli strains)

precautions: Do not over-incubate beyond the standard reading window, or a false alkaline reversion of the slant can be misread as a negative for lactose/sucrose fermentation.
Loosen the cap slightly to allow some aeration for correct slant-surface reactions.
limitations: Interpretation requires reading multiple features together; a single feature in isolation (e.g. color alone) can be misleading without the full pattern.
